title: G26 format-scoped lexical retrieval prospective evaluation
goal: Validate JavaScript/TypeScript filtered parity and mixed JavaScript/TypeScript/Rust relevance after Rust joins the shared code corpus.
checkout_policy: Both arms index the same clean checkout pinned to corpus_revision. The baseline binary is built from baseline_revision and ignores Rust; the treatment binary is built from treatment_revision.

execution.binary_build: cargo build --release --locked in a separately validated clean binary-source checkout
execution.database_policy: Each arm requires a fresh external database path and a fresh output path.
execution.scope_validation: Every filtered-parity raw hit must be JavaScript or TypeScript. Mixed raw hits may use any registered code format.
execution.snapshot_policy: Every query response within one arm must carry the same nonempty snapshot. Baseline and treatment snapshots are not compared because their indexed memberships differ.
execution.runner_provenance: Each report records the runner path and SHA-256; treatment accepts a baseline report only when its runner SHA-256 matches the current runner bytes.
execution.baseline: Run only filtered_parity_queries with the baseline binary and no unsupported --format arguments.
execution.treatment_filtered_parity: Run filtered_parity_queries with repeated --format javascript --format typescript arguments.

ranking_unit: Retain 100 raw ranked chunk hits, deduplicate files by first chunk position, then truncate to 10 files.

metric_policy.filtered_parity: Macro-average file Recall@10 and reciprocal rank over all 24 controls; also track every baseline top-five judged-gold file.
metric_policy.mixed_relevance: Pooled-judgment mean graded nDCG@10 using gain 2^grade-1. Unjudged returned files receive gain zero only for metric computation: they are not declared irrelevant.
metric_policy.language_representation: Observe and report returned formats for mixed queries, but never enforce a language quota.

source_holdout.title: Prospective G26 v3 source-authored holdout

grading_scale.1: supporting context that is relevant but not sufficient on its own
grading_scale.2: substantial participant in transport, orchestration, validation, or persistence
grading_scale.3: direct and authoritative implementation or contract for the requested behavior

source_holdout.judgment_policy: gold_files contains every grade 2 or 3 file. Grade 1 files remain explicit supporting judgments. Unjudged files are not asserted irrelevant.
